data.name: Jesus
data.gender_notes: Jesus is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In the New Testament of the Bible, Jesus is the name of the son of God and the central figure of Christianity. He is believed to have been born of the virgin Mary and to have lived a sinless life, died on the cross as an atonement for sin, and rose from the dead three days later. The name Jesus carries the meaning “Savior, Deliverer” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Jesus usually hope their child will grow to embody savior, deliverer and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Jesus represents love, forgiveness, and salvation.
data.etymology: Jesus belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Savior, Deliverer.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Jesus total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

in_latin.name: Jesus
in_latin.long_meaning: Jesus nomen sacerdotale significans salvatorem mundi, a Iesu Iudaismo originis, per Ioannis Evangelium in Novo Testamento scripturae scriptum est. Iesu nomen in Ecclesia Christiana usitatum est, Christo Salvatore mundi significans. Iesu nomen a Sancta Trinitate, a Patre et Spiritu Sancto originis, in Ecclesia Christiana celebratur.

in_english.name: Jesus
in_english.meaning: name of savior, anointed one, messiah, god's gift, savior of the world
in_english.long_meaning: Jesus name of savior, anointed one, messiah, god's gift, savior of the world, comes from Hebrew Iesu, meaning 'God's gift' or 'salvation', via John's Gospel in the New Testament scripture. Jesus name in the Christian Church is used, meaning the Christ, savior of the world. Jesus name originates from the Holy Trinity, from the Father and the Holy Spirit, celebrated in the Christian Church.

data.cultural_impact: Jesus is a figure of immense significance in Western culture. The story of Jesus' life, death, and resurrection is the basis of Christianity, which influences and shapes the lives of over 2.4 billion people worldwide. Jesus has also been a subject of innumerable works of art, literature, and music. From "The Last Supper" to Handel's "Messiah," Jesus' story continues to inspire and captivate people of all walks of life.
data.spiritual_significance: In Christian belief, Jesus is the Savior and Redeemer who took on the sins of humanity and provided a way for individuals to be reconciled with God. He is honored as the Son of God, the Prince of Peace, and the embodiment of love and compassion. Christians believe that through faith in Jesus, they can receive forgiveness for their sins and live in a right relationship with God. For many, the name of Jesus carries deep spiritual significance as a symbol of hope, grace, and love.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Jesus, meaning "Savior" or "Deliverer" in Hebrew, symbolizes the divine figure who brings salvation, hope, and redemption to humanity. His name represents the embodiment of God's love and grace, offering forgiveness and a path to eternal life.

biblical_reference.note: Iesu name in the New Testament scripture, referring to Jesus Christ, the savior of the world.
